split_reasoning: Organizing and writing material are steps in completing the same writing assignment.

parts.text: Organize and write assigned technical material to the prescribed standards.
parts.type_reasoning: Each assignment produces a draft or completed piece of technical writing.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assigned document or section is handed over as a whole for review or publication.
parts.work_item: one assigned technical document or section
parts.start: writing assignment and applicable standards received
parts.end: completed draft submitted for review or publication
parts.checked_by: editor, technical reviewer, or publication manager

notes: Online help writing can also be an assignment under this statement.

split_reasoning: Maintaining records and files of work and revisions is one recordkeeping activity.

parts.text: Maintain the records and files for a technical writing assignment and its revisions.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces an updated set of files that colleagues can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A set of updates to an assignment's files can be completed and made available together.
parts.work_item: one assignment's work and revision files updated
parts.start: new work or revision ready to be recorded and filed
parts.end: files and revision records updated in the designated repository

split_reasoning: Editing, standardizing, and changing others' material are alternative forms of the same document-editing activity.

parts.text: Edit and standardize technical material prepared by another writer or employee.
parts.type_reasoning: Each editing assignment produces revised material for review or use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A document or assigned section is returned as a whole with its changes.
parts.start: other person's material received for editing
parts.end: edited material returned or submitted for review
parts.checked_by: original author, editor, or publication manager

notes: Editing existing online help can also be covered by task 20243.

split_reasoning: The listed parties are alternative participants in the same requirements discussion.

parts.text: Confer with stakeholders to establish technical specifications and publication subject matter.
parts.type_reasoning: The task is a live exchange to establish requirements, rather than a specified written deliverable.

notes: A separately prepared specification is not explicit in the target.

split_reasoning: Reviewing published material and recommending changes form one review activity.

parts.text: Review a publication and recommend changes to its content, scope, format, or production.
parts.type_reasoning: The review produces recommendations for a publication decision.
parts.unit_reasoning: Recommendations are made for a particular publication or assigned portion and handed to a decision-maker.
parts.work_item: one publication review with recommended changes
parts.start: published material selected or assigned for review

notes: The target covers recommending changes, not necessarily implementing them.

split_reasoning: The listed visual forms are alternative illustrations selected for the same purpose.

parts.type_reasoning: The selection produces a set of visuals for the material.
parts.unit_reasoning: The illustrations selected for an assigned document or section are handed over for review and layout together.
parts.work_item: one document or section's illustration selection
parts.start: material and candidate visuals available for selection
parts.end: selected visuals identified or supplied for review and layout
parts.checked_by: editor, technical reviewer, or layout specialist

notes: Selecting visuals may occur during layout, but it does not necessarily include laying out the publication.

split_reasoning: Drawings, specifications, mockups, and samples are inputs to the same study of technical and procedural details.

parts.text: Study technical inputs to identify technology, operating procedures, and production sequences for documentation.
parts.type_reasoning: The study can produce a documented account of the technical details needed for writing.
parts.unit_reasoning: Findings for an assigned product, procedure, or section can be collected as one research record for the writing team.
parts.work_item: one set of technical research notes for an assigned topic
parts.start: drawings, specifications, mockups, or samples made available for study
parts.end: relevant technical and procedural details documented for use in writing

notes: Research notes may be informal or incorporated directly into a draft rather than handed over separately.

split_reasoning: Interviewing personnel and independently reading background material are different activities.

parts.text: Interview production or engineering personnel to learn about products and production methods.
parts.type_reasoning: The specified activity is a live information-gathering interaction, not a separately specified deliverable.

parts.text: Read journals and other background material to become familiar with product technologies and production methods.
parts.type_reasoning: Background reading for familiarity does not itself produce a specified item for others to check or rely on.

notes: The time split is an estimate; interview notes or a research summary are not specified by the target.

split_reasoning: Observing production, development, and experiments serves the same purpose of determining procedural details.

parts.text: Observe activities to determine operating procedures and details for documentation.
parts.type_reasoning: An observation can produce recorded procedural findings for use in technical material.
parts.unit_reasoning: The findings from observing an assigned operation or activity can be collected as one record for the documentation team.
parts.work_item: one set of observed procedure notes
parts.start: operation or activity selected and made available for observation
parts.end: observed sequence and relevant details recorded for documentation
parts.checked_by: technical writer, operator, or technical reviewer

notes: The target does not explicitly require written notes; findings may instead be incorporated directly into a draft.

split_reasoning: Arranging typing, duplication, and distribution coordinates the handling of the same material.

parts.text: Arrange the typing, duplication, and distribution needed for technical material.
parts.type_reasoning: The coordination produces an instruction or order for the people handling the material.
parts.unit_reasoning: The arrangements for a particular document or batch can be communicated as one production request.
parts.work_item: one document production and distribution request
parts.end: necessary arrangements communicated to the responsible staff or vendor
parts.checked_by: production or distribution staff, vendor, or publication manager

notes: An arrangement may cover only some of the listed services.

split_reasoning: Assisting with publication layout is one activity.

parts.text: Assist in laying out technical material for publication.
parts.type_reasoning: Layout work produces a formatted document or section for review.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assigned document or section is formatted and passed on as a whole.
parts.start: text, visuals, and layout requirements received
parts.end: layout or proof submitted for review
parts.checked_by: editor, layout specialist, or publication manager

split_reasoning: Assessing whether developments require revisions or new material is one analysis activity with related possible recommendations.

parts.text: Analyze field developments and recommend whether documentation needs revision or new material.
parts.type_reasoning: The analysis produces an assessment that publication planners can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assessment of a development or group of developments is communicated as a decision input.
parts.end: assessment of needed revisions or new material communicated
parts.checked_by: publication manager, editor, or subject-matter lead

notes: Some monitoring may be informal; the coded item is the assessment used to make a documentation decision.

split_reasoning: Catalogs, drawings, and other data are alternative sources reviewed for equipment operation, maintenance, and service information.

parts.text: Review equipment sources for operation, maintenance, and service information.
parts.type_reasoning: A targeted review can produce research findings for equipment documentation.
parts.unit_reasoning: Information gathered for an assigned equipment topic can be recorded and used as one research set.
parts.work_item: one set of equipment-source research notes
parts.start: equipment topic and relevant source materials identified
parts.end: relevant operation, maintenance, and service information recorded for use
parts.checked_by: technical writer or equipment subject-matter expert

notes: The target does not explicitly require a separate research record; findings may be used directly in writing.

split_reasoning: Sketches may be drawn by hand away from a computer or created digitally, so the physical and computer work are separated.

parts.text: Draw a sketch by hand to illustrate material or an assembly sequence.
parts.type_reasoning: Hand drawing on paper requires physical work away from a computer.

parts.text: Create a digital sketch to illustrate material or an assembly sequence.
parts.type_reasoning: A digital sketch is a distinct illustration produced at a computer.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each illustration is supplied as a whole for technical review or inclusion in material.
parts.start: illustration requirement and technical inputs received
parts.end: sketch submitted for review or inclusion
parts.checked_by: technical reviewer, editor, or layout specialist

notes: The hand-versus-digital split and shares depend on the workplace and illustration tools.

split_reasoning: Developing and maintaining online help both produce or update help content; the unit is an assigned help topic or section.

parts.text: Develop or update online help documentation.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a new or revised help topic for review and publication.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assigned help topic or section can be reviewed and published as a whole.
parts.work_item: one online help topic or section created or updated
parts.start: documentation request, change requirement, or assigned topic received
parts.end: help content submitted for review or published
parts.checked_by: editor, product specialist, and end users

notes: A larger help system is normally completed through multiple topics or sections.
